issues.description: Method Milkable.messageOnMilk(): The problem statement (UML and Part 2) specifies messageOnMilk() should return a String with the text "[Animal Type] [name] is milked". In the solution, the Milkable interface declares messageOnMilk() as returning boolean, and the implementing classes (Goat and Seal) implement public boolean messageOnMilk() by printing the milk message and returning true. This contradicts the problem specification (String return) and will confuse students about the correct method signature and expected behavior, and can cause tests that expect a String-returning method to fail or be incompatible.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the problem statement: change the Milkable interface to declare String messageOnMilk(); then update Goat and Seal to return the formatted String (e.g. "Goat Buttinsky is milked") instead of printing and returning a boolean. Update any callers (e.g. Main or tests) to print or use the returned String. Alternatively, if a boolean return was intentional, update the problem statement and UML to document the boolean return and adjust textual instructions — but prefer making the code match the stated specification (String) to avoid student confusion.
